fields.features_heading: The Questions That Set a Moving Price
fields.features_subheading: Emergent turns your price list into a moving quote form that names a number before anyone picks up the phone.
fields.feature_1:
Movers and hours set by home size

Set how many movers and hours each home size takes, plus your hourly rate. The form multiplies them as the customer answers and shows the estimate before the request is sent.
fields.feature_2:
Flat fees for pianos and safes

List the items that need extra hands or equipment, each with its own fee. A ticked upright piano or gun safe joins the estimate as its own line, and the customer sees what it adds.
fields.feature_3:
Stairs and elevators at both ends

Ask about flights of stairs, elevator access, and the walk from the truck to the door at each address. Those answers add time to the estimate instead of surprising the crew.
fields.feature_4:
Requests that reach the right person

Post office moves to a Slack channel and email home moves to the owner, each with its answers and estimate. The customer gets a copy of the quote by email once the request is saved.
fields.feature_5:
A request board sorted by move day

Every request lands as a row in a database you own, with its status and move date. Set a rush window, and each request inside it carries a Rush mark at the top of the board.
fields.feature_6:
The code, in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. A developer can place the quote form inside the moving company's existing site and keep building on it there.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Movers Quote Their Jobs
fields.tab_content_1:
Five hours with 3 movers comes to $825

Imogen Tavallai is leaving a 2-bedroom apartment on June 14. Corliss Street Movers' form asks for the move date and the home size, and a 2-bedroom gets 3 movers for 5 hours. At $165 an hour for the crew and truck, she sees an $825 estimate before she submits. Her request is saved with her answers.
fields.tab_content_2:
One piano and one safe lift Teodor's quote to $995

Rookwood Moving Co. prices heavy items as flat fees on top of the move. Teodor Vashti books a 1-bedroom move at $540 and ticks an upright piano and a gun safe. The form adds $275 for the piano and $180 for the safe, then emails him a $995 quote with each fee on its own line.
fields.tab_content_3:
Eighteen workstations at $70 each, plus the server rack

Saltmarsh Accounting is changing floors on a Saturday and asks Kittredge Commercial Moving for a quote. The form prices 18 workstations at $70 each and adds $350 for the server rack, $1,610 in all. The request posts to the #commercial-moves channel in Slack with the move day and the workstation count.
fields.tab_content_4:
Requests 7 days or less from move day go first

Late May is busy at Ashgrove Movers. Owner Delphine Arkwright opens the request board and finds 3 open requests. Any request 7 days or less from move day is marked Rush and moves to the top. Wynn Castellane moves in 3 days and sits first, while the moves 12 and 26 days out stay Quoted.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Moving Quote Form
fields.howto_description: Turn the way you price moves by phone into a moving quote form, then build and test it with Emergent in seven steps.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down how you price a job today
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about the hard parts of a move
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Price heavy items on their own
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the move date near the top
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull the last ten moves you quoted by phone and note the crew size and hours for each, plus the rate you charged. That list becomes the form's math. If you charge a flat price for some jobs, write those down too.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List what makes a move take longer: the home size, flights of stairs, a long walk from the truck, an elevator that has to be reserved. Each one becomes a question on the form, and each answer adds time to the estimate.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give pianos, safes, and pool tables flat fees instead of folding them into the hourly rate. The customer ticks what they own, and the estimate lists each fee separately. Nobody is surprised when the crew shows up with a piano dolly.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for the move date before anything else, because crew booking and follow-up both depend on it. Pick a rush window for moves that are close, and requests inside it can go straight to the top of your board.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put your rates and questions into one prompt, fees included. Emergent builds the moving quote form, the database behind it, and the request board. When a rate changes in the busy season, ask for the change in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Choose who hears about each request
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide where each kind of request goes. Home moves might email the owner, while office moves post to a Slack channel the commercial crew reads. Send the customer a copy of the estimate to keep the number in writing.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with three kinds of move
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form as a customer would for a studio, a 3-bedroom house with a piano, and an office floor. Check each estimate against what you would have quoted by phone, and fix any rate that comes out wrong.

faq_plan.q: What is a moving quote form?
faq_plan.a: A moving quote form is the online form a moving company uses to collect the details of a move and give the customer a price or an estimate. It collects the move date and the size of the home, plus anything that adds time, such as stairs or a piano.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a moving quote form?
faq_plan.a: Write down how you price moves today: your hourly crew rate and the fees for heavy items. Describe those rates and the questions you ask by phone to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form and its estimate math, with a database of every request, and you change any of it by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a moving quote form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with the move date, both addresses, and the home size. Those three decide how many movers you send and for how long. Then ask about stairs, elevators, and parking at each address. Finish with heavy items such as a piano or a safe, and an email address for the estimate.

faq_plan.q: Should a moving quote form show an exact price or an estimate?
faq_plan.a: Show an estimate for hourly moves, and say what it rests on: the crew size and the hours. Keep exact prices for flat-fee items such as a piano, where the price does not change with time. The same split works on a construction quote form, where small jobs get a number and large ones get a visit.

faq_plan.q: How does a moving quote form estimate crew hours?
faq_plan.a: Start from your own past jobs. Average the hours your crews took for each home size, such as a studio or a 2-bedroom, and note the crew size that went with them. The form multiplies those hours by your hourly rate. Emergent keeps every request and its estimate in a database you own, ready to compare with the hours each move took.

faq_plan.q: How should a moving quote form price pianos and other heavy items?
faq_plan.a: Price them as flat fees on their own lines, separate from the hourly estimate. Name the items that take extra crew or equipment, such as an upright piano, a gun safe, or a pool table, and give each one a price. Ask where the item sits, too: a piano on a second floor takes more work than one by the front door.

faq_plan.q: What should happen after a customer submits a moving quote form?
faq_plan.a: The request is saved, the right person hears about it, and the customer gets the estimate by email. If you also clean homes after a move, link a separate cleaning quote form from the confirmation screen for customers who want both. A request board then shows which requests still need a call.

faq_plan.q: Can a moving quote form handle long-distance moves?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but quote it on a different basis than an hourly local move. Collect a room-by-room inventory and both ZIP codes, then follow up with a video or in-home survey before you give a firm price. Mark long-distance requests on the board for whoever handles those moves.

faq_plan.q: How do I ask about stairs and elevators on a moving quote form?
faq_plan.a: Ask the same questions for both addresses: the floor, the number of flights, whether there is an elevator, and whether it has to be reserved. Add how far the truck can park from the door. Each answer can add a set amount of time to the estimate, and Emergent builds that math from your description, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Does a moving quote form work for large office relocations?
faq_plan.a: For a small office, yes: price per workstation and add fees for server racks or file rooms. A large relocation run as a formal bid needs more than a quote can hold, such as a schedule and insurance details. A proposal form fits that better, with room for each section the bid asks for.

plan.angle: The keyword has 20 searches a month and no ranked top 10 in the workbook, and the AlsoAsked tree is about tipping and cheap movers, so the page wins on usefulness to the mover who builds the form: template pages stop at name, addresses and a notes box, which leaves the owner to call back for the home size. This page shows the questions that actually set a moving price (home size and crew hours, specialty items, workstations for office moves, the move date) across four jobs: an hourly local move estimated on screen, a piano and safe priced as flat fees and emailed, an office move priced per workstation and posted to Slack, and a request board that puts requests 7 days or less from move day at the top. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, the questions to ask, estimate versus exact price, crew hours, heavy items, what happens after submit, long-distance moves, stairs and elevators, and large office relocations.
